question: There are three isotopes of hydrogen atom, namely Protium, Deuterium and Tritium. The respective atomic number and mass number of the isotope Tritium is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1,3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tritium** is one of the isotopes of hydrogen.
 
• The atomic number of hydrogen, including its** isotopes, is 1** (since all hydrogen isotopes have one proton).
 
• Tritium has **2 neutrons in addition to the 1 proton**, giving it a mass number of 3 (1 proton + 2 neutrons = 3).
 
• Tritium is radioactive, with a half-life of about 12.32 years, decaying into **helium-3 (³He) **through beta decay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protium** (¹H) Atomic Number: 1 Mass Number: 1
 
• It is the **most common isotope of hydrogen**, making up about 99.98% of naturally occurring hydrogen.
 
• **Deuterium** (²H or D)Atomic Number: 1 Mass Number: 2.
 
• Deuterium has **1 proton and 1 neutron** in its nucleus. It makes up about 0.02% of naturally occurring hydrogen.
 
• **Tritium** (³H or T) Atomic Number: 1 Mass Number: 3
 
• Tritium has **1 proton and 2 neutrons** in its nucleus.
 
• Tritium is much rarer than the other two isotopes and occurs naturally in trace amounts (about 1 part in 1 trillion of hydrogen).
